summary: June 2024 systematic-investor episode: a choppy period where trend managers gave back about half of Q1 gains, answers on CFD costs and ATR sizing, then Brennan summarizes a 2023 paper deriving optimal trend rules via Markov and semi-Markov regime models that matches practitioners backtests, and argues AI threatens short-term but not medium/long-term trend following.

coverage.note: Fed repricing, trend giveback, rebalance into trend
trend barometer, index returns, CFD cost structure
backtest costs, ATR sizing across price levels
paper intro, using LLMs to read papers
ad hoc optimization vs math, paper findings
MACD optimal, dynamic adjustment, forecast horizon
AI and short-term competition, core rules
capacity and market impact, CTA edge vs AI

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: I'm referring to it as a pogos stic environment at the moment
claims.claim: A choppy pogo-stick market with many whipsaws produces successes in some assets and failures in others, a hard period for trend models.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's not going to be that easy to get rid of inflation and high for longer
claims.claim: The Fed dot plot moved from several cuts to maybe one, and Niels thinks inflation is sticky (high for longer) and the next move might even be a hike, leaving markets without a clear path.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: maybe half of q1's returns have been uh given back by managers
claims.claim: Trend managers had given back about half of Q1 returns, broad-based across metals, fixed income and currencies, which is not unusual for trend following.
claims.conditions: drawdowns of this size are normal for trend

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: maybe it's time to reverse that uh equation and rebalance back into Trend
claims.claim: After allocators rebalanced out of trend following following its 2022 win, stocks at all-time highs and trend in a drawdown may be a good point to rebalance back into trend as a diversifier.
claims.direction: increase trend allocation after a drawdown with equities at highs
claims.conditions: trend has lagged and equities near highs

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: finished at 27 yesterday so that's a pretty weak reading so completely in line with the returns we see
claims.claim: A trend barometer reading of 27 indicates a weak trend environment, consistent with the poor CTA returns.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: stock gen CTA down 2.16 % uh for June
claims.claim: Reported mid-June 2024 returns: SG CTA -2.16% for the month and +7.15% YTD, SG Trend -2.5% and +8.89%, short-term traders -2% and +0.69%, versus MSCI World +10.58% and S&P 500 +14.65% YTD.
claims.indicator: SG CTA, SG Trend, SG Short-Term Traders, MSCI World, S&P 500

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: there'll be holding costs which in our world of cfds we call swap costs
claims.claim: CFD trading carries broker spreads, slippage and holding (swap) costs, which are larger than futures costs and depend on broker margin-making rather than centralized exchanges.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: has positive swap on top of the the trend value we've got the the benefit of the carry trade
claims.claim: When the trend direction has positive swap the trade earns carry on top of trend; the swap differs by asset and direction.
claims.direction: trade trend direction with positive swap
claims.conditions: holding period long enough to accrue swap
claims.testable: yes - add swap carry to trend backtest

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: if you're holding for extended periods the cost of that um swap can become quite large
claims.claim: Trends in assets with negative swap make long holds expensive, so swap costs can materially reduce performance and should be monitored on a dashboard.
claims.direction: avoid long holds on negative-swap markets

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: then once that test is done you need to import back the costs associated with your broker
claims.claim: Backtest first for trend suitability, then add actual broker costs, which may eliminate some markets or models as untradeable.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: I risk per trade let's say an example of $500 per trade
claims.claim: When prices and ATR rise several-fold over decades, keep a constant dollar risk per trade (stop = multiple of 25-day ATR) and let contract counts change; large early position counts are expected, not a bug.
claims.indicator: 25-period ATR; fixed dollar risk per trade
claims.conditions: long backtests where price level and vol change

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: download the PDF from that white paper into chat GPT
claims.claim: Use an LLM to read and explain academic quant papers to lay readers step by step.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: the methods that they deploy to come up with their models tends to be what they refer to as ad hoc
claims.claim: The 2023 paper (Optimal trend following rules in two-state switching regime models) says trend followers build models by ad hoc heavy optimization and proposes mathematical formulas (Markov processes, autoregression) to derive optimal models.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: actually agree with the optimal models that for instance you and I come to with our back testing process
claims.claim: The mathematically optimal models are simple, medium-to-long-term holds with loose parameter sets, matching those found through practitioner backtesting.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: found that on unseen data they were very effective models that got him a sharp of about 1.2
claims.claim: Stark applied the equity-derived optimal parameters to futures on unseen data and got a Sharpe ratio of about 1.2 over 20-30 years.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: it's using the data as opposed to our assumptions as to what those states are
claims.claim: A Markov model infers a chosen number of market states from the data via Bayesian inference, giving the probability of being in each state and a transition matrix, which may not match bull/bear labels.
claims.conditions: number of states chosen by the researcher

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: we can use our Trend following models as a bit like thermometers
claims.claim: In a hidden Markov model, trend-model returns act as thermometers of the market state, giving state-dependent weights per model and a short-term forecast of the next state.
claims.indicator: returns of long-only, short-only, mean-reverting models as state observations

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: the longer you are in a trend the greater the chance that trend is going to end
claims.claim: Trend strength waxes and wanes via autocorrelation, and the longer a trend persists the greater the chance it ends, which a strict Markov model cannot represent.
claims.direction: trend exit hazard rises with age

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: how those transition probabilities change over the course of time as that Trend endures
claims.claim: A semi-Markov model lets transition probabilities change with trend duration, giving both model allocation and when to switch between models.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: they're mathematically equivalent
claims.claim: Autoregression (serial correlation across many lags) and Markov models are mathematically equivalent views of the same trend persistence, so moving-average, EMA, MACD and momentum rules can be optimized analytically.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: the EMA was the best model to use in trending environments
claims.claim: Under a plain Markov two-state model the exponential moving average was the best trend rule.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: they found that actually the macd model was the better model
claims.claim: Under the more realistic semi-Markov model MACD was the best rule, with optimal parameters matching what practitioners find.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: often late to enter a trend and early to leave a trend
claims.claim: Short-term regime forecasts from Markov models could let trend models adjust dynamically to reduce late entry and early exit from trends.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: predictive certainty about what's the next Market regime is a very shortterm um finding
claims.claim: Regime prediction is only reliable over a very short horizon (days to a week), like weather forecasts out to about 14 days, and decays quickly afterwards.
claims.conditions: ML and AI methods; beyond one week the accuracy fades

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: keep away from that short-term space because that short-term space with AI advancements
claims.claim: To avoid competing with AI, favor medium-to-long-term trends, since the short-term space will become much more competitive as AI improves.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: maybe it could calculate what what would the optimal position size be at any given time
claims.claim: Niels speculates the same methods could extend to optimal position sizing, and says his firm already uses dynamic parameter selection.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Trend following following the core principles that we always come back to uh still seems to be working very well
claims.claim: Technology advances repeatedly predicted the end of trend following, yet core rules have worked for 50 years; AI is a helpful tool, not a revolution.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: operates um particularly in the shortterm time frame you know from one day to one week
claims.claim: Medallion operates on one-day to one-week horizons using many data sources and Markov models with a top-level allocator by market state.
claims.testable: no - external claim about a private fund

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: why is it that they could make so much money in Medallion but they couldn't make any money for their external clients
claims.claim: Niels questions why the same technology did not beat benchmarks for Renaissance external funds.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: he knew he couldn't add any more aom to his existing models because the market impact of those models would get too significant
claims.claim: Short-term high-alpha models have capacity limits from market impact; the scalable external equity fund used medium-to-long-term trend models and performed only marginally.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: in the medium to long-term space I honestly think that if there's anyone out here who's got a competive Advantage news it's us the ctas
claims.claim: AI will quickly take over short-term prediction, but CTAs have the advantage in medium-to-long-term trends; mean reversion and HFT are more at risk.
claims.direction: trend following over mean reversion and HFT

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if there's one thing you shouldn't do is to do Trend following on a single sector uh or single Market it doesn't work
claims.claim: Trend following works only when diversified across many markets and sectors; single-market trend following does not work.
